title: Moss rose – the other portulaca
scope: 2026 UF/IFAS Charlotte County article states Portulaca grandiflora (moss rose) is not edible and distinguishes it from P. oleracea cultivated as a vegetable; it also reports pet toxicity. This conflicts with NC State's species page listing flowers and seeds as edible and Wisconsin Extension listing seeds as edible; the UF/IFAS article itself cites both sources in its resource list while still concluding moss rose is not edible. It gives no human-toxicity mechanism, so the source relationship does not resolve the conflicting human-edibility claims.
